follow100Note: Of every $100 Coinbase took in, its running costs came to $101.65 — the quarter only ended in profit because paper gains on its investments added $123.45. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Coinbase reports no gross-profit line; 'Transaction expense' — the direct cost of processing trades — is shown as cost of revenue. The core business made a $25M operating loss this quarter, so the chart has no operating-profit step: the investment gains (shown as other income) cover the small shortfall, pay the tax bill, and make up the net profit. 'Other operating expense, net' of $299M nets a $9M gain on crypto held for operations against $308M of other operating costs, substantially all data-theft incident costs. Figures are from Coinbase's Q2 2025 shareholder letter (Exhibit 99.1) and Form 10-Q.

oneTimers: A roughly $1.5B pre-tax gain on strategic investments, mostly an unrealized mark-up of Coinbase's stake in Circle after its June 2025 IPO — non-cash.
A $362M pre-tax gain on crypto assets held for investment — largely unrealized.

otherDetail: A $1,507M gain on strategic investments — mostly the Circle stake — plus a $362M gain on crypto held as an investment, less $21M of interest expense: a net $1,848M. These paper gains are why a quarter with an operating loss still shows a large net profit.

takeaways.text: Coinbase's stake in Circle — the stablecoin company that went public in June — was marked up by about $1.5B, and the crypto it holds as an investment gained another $362M. Neither is cash, and both reverse if prices fall: adjusted net income, which strips both out, was just $33M.
takeaways.title: A paper gain did the heavy lifting

takeaways.text: Revenue fell 26% from the first quarter to $1.50B as crypto volatility — the fuel of trading fees — dropped. Transaction revenue fell 39% to $764M, while subscription and services revenue held up better, slipping 6% to $656M.
takeaways.title: Trading cooled from Q1

takeaways.text: Other operating costs were $308M, substantially all tied to the May 2025 data-theft incident — customer reimbursements, remediation and legal costs. That one item is what pushed the core business to a $25M operating loss.
takeaways.title: The data-theft bill arrived

verdict: Coinbase's core business ran at a small operating loss in a quieter crypto quarter — revenue fell 26% from Q1 as trading cooled — but paper gains on its investments, above all a roughly $1.5B mark-up on its Circle stake, turned the quarter into a $1.43B net profit.
